summary.text: Josh Seckinger is a Democratic member of the Montana House of Representatives who has represented District 62 since January 2025 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026, against Republican Esther Fishbaugh.
A fly-fishing guide by profession, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that he has lived in Bozeman since 2009.

paragraphs.text: Seckinger studied political science and geography at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, according to his 2026 Ballotpedia survey answers.
In that survey he said he was raised by a single mother and has spent more than a decade working as a professional fly-fishing guide.
Ballotpedia lists earlier work in seismic mapping, food distribution, newspaper printing and construction labor.
Seckinger first won the seat in 2024, defeating Republican Owen Lang 51.1 percent to 48.9 percent after winning the Democratic primary over Rio Roland.
In the 2025-2026 session he was assigned to the House Natural Resources, Fish, Wildlife and Parks, and Business and Labor committees.
He advanced unopposed from the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary.
In his 2026 survey, Seckinger listed affordability for working people, protection of public lands, clean water and public access, and practical, independent representation as his key messages.
He also named property-tax reform, housing, health-care costs, strong public schools and responsible energy policy as areas of interest.
